title: The resource hierarchy: organisation, folders, projects and resources

videos.script: Everything in Google Cloud lives somewhere in one tree. {{tree}} At the top is the organisation. That is the company, tied to its domain. Under it sit folders, and folders can hold more folders. {{folders}} Then come projects. A project is not a drawer for tidiness. It is a wall. It has its own APIs, its own quotas, its own bill and its own permissions. {{wall}} And every resource lives in exactly one project. A topic, a network, a machine. {{resources}} The tree matters because rules flow down it. Grant a role on a folder, and every project under it has that grant. {{inherit}} In your lab, you will see the project inside a name. Two topics called orders, in two projects, and neither knows the other. {{names}} Then you write the whole tree as Terraform, three folders and five projects. You ask Terraform what it would do. It answers without asking Google anything. {{plan}} And you learn what that answer leaves out. {{end}}
